thread:
maria: FYI — noticed a cluster of 503/stream-abort errors hitting the gateway during a short auth refresh window at 03:12 UTC. Patterns look like: short requests unaffected, long streaming sessions see midstream auth refresh and then either drop or queue for a long time.
cheng: Can you paste a sample trace? Is it the token refresh that stalls the ingress handshake?
maria: Trace: `gateway:session=abc123 -> auth: refresh start 03:12:04 -> upstream handshake delay 03:12:06 -> client keepalive 03:12:10 -> stream aborted by proxy`
maria: Also saw `ERR: auth: 401->401 retry loop` in the auth service logs.
devon: Hmm. Two likely failure modes: 1) auth refresh blocks the route handler thread, delaying trailers handshake; 2) gateway's admission queue lumps streaming requests behind auth-bound short calls and hits the queue timeout.
sara: We recently bumped ingress concurrency limits on the frontdoor to favor throughput. Might have exposed an ordering issue where token refresh RPCs hog the pool.
cheng: If refresh RPCs are synchronous on the hot path, they can stall KV cache / session-thread which we use for stream prevalidation. Proposal: decouple auth refresh into async background punch-through — allow an optimistic short-lived session to continue streaming while refresh proceeds, with a safety TTL.
devon: +1 on optimistic path, but we need side effects safety. For idempotency and billing we can't re-allow arbitrary long-running streams without ensuring token scope hasn't changed. Maybe: allow continuation for N seconds (config) and annotate trace with `auth-degraded:true`. If final refresh fails, mark session as soft-ended and emit trailers indicating potential stale auth.
maria: Ops concern — we already surface `client-visible errors` for midstream auth fail. If we change to soft annotations we'll need UI and client contract updates. Is that acceptable?
sara: We can gate behind a feature flag per-tenant. Enterprise customers can opt-out if they require strict midstream auth enforcement. Default for hosted tier: optimistic continuation with 10s grace.
cheng: Implementation notes: 1) introduce `auth_grace_seconds` in frontdoor route config (default 10). 2) when refresh in flight, mark session proto `AuthGrace: true` and set watch to abort if refresh fails after grace window. 3) emit event `edge.auth.grace.start` / `edge.auth.grace.end` for observability.
devon: Also tweak admission queue priority: treat in-flight streaming continuations as higher priority than new short requests once they hold a stream token, to avoid eviction. This prevents churn where short auth refresh calls keep evicting streaming slots.
maria: Could this interact badly with bursty tenant traffic (DDoS-like)? We should add a per-tenant cap on how many optimistic continuations are allowed.
sara: Agreed. Configs: `tenant.auth_grace_limit` + global `auth_grace_ratio` to avoid capacity exhaustion.
cheng: Pseudo-config snippet: ```yaml route: /v1/stream: auth_grace_seconds: 10 auth_grace_limit_per_tenant: 5 auth_grace_ratio: 0.05 ```
devon: Observability checklist: counters for grace started/failed/succeeded, histogram of grace durations, trace tag propagation so APM can filter. Also an alert on >1% of streams hitting grace and then failing.
maria: Can someone drive a small RFC + rollout plan? Steps: spec -> unit tests (auth mocking) -> canary on a single region -> feature flag + opt-out for Dedicated customers -> wide rollout.
sara: I'll own the rollout plan. I'll add guardrails for Dedicated customers.
cheng: I'll draft the RFC with config defaults and API changes (trailer semantics). We'll need SDK notes about `edge.auth.degraded` trailer.
ops-bot: Deploy pipeline check: `canary` env has 12/12 healthy nodes, no pending deploys. Ready for RFC staging once authored. :white_check_mark:
maria: Thanks — sync tomorrow 10:00 to review RFC and clarify client contract text. :thumbsup:
